messages.content: I'm planning a series of long weekend getaways for the upcoming year and I need to know when they'll occur in my country. Could you fetch me the list of long weekends for Canada in the year 2023? I'd like to integrate this information into my holiday planning app.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of **Canadian statutory holidays that produced “long weekends”** during 2023. (“Long weekend” here means a holiday that either lands on a weekday adjacent to a weekend *or* is officially observed on a weekday that turns a normal weekend into a multi‑day break.) | Date | Holiday | Weekday | How it made a long weekend | |------|---------|--------|----------------------------| | **Jan 02** | New Year’s Day (observation) | Monday | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday Jan 01 → observed Monday Jan 02, giving a 4‑day stretch (Sat Dec 30–Mon Jan 02). | | **Feb 20** | Family Day (most provinces) | Monday | Third Monday of February → standard 4‑day weekend (Fri Feb 17–Mon Feb 20). | | **Apr 07** | Good Friday | Friday | Directly a holiday → Fri‑Sun long weekend (Apr 07–09). | | **May 22** | Victoria Day | Monday | First Monday of June → 4‑day weekend (Fri Jun 02–Mon May 22). | | **Jul 03** | Canada Day (observation) | Monday | Canada Day fell on Saturday Jul 01 → observed Monday Jul 03, creating a 4‑day break (Fri Jun 30–Mon Jul 03). | | **Sep 04** | Labour Day | Monday | Standard first Monday of September → 4‑day weekend (Fri Aug 31–Mon Sep 04). | | **Oct 09** | Thanksgiving | Monday | First Monday of October → 4‑day weekend (Fri Oct 06–Mon Oct 09). | | **Nov 11** | Remembrance Day *(paid holiday in most provinces)* | Thursday | Falls on Thursday → Thurs‑Sun long weekend (Thu Nov 10–Sun Nov 12). | ### Notes & Caveats | Item | Explanation | |------|-------------| | **Provincial Variations** | • Family Day is celebrated in Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, British Columbia, Newfoundland & Labrador, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and New Brunswick.
• Québec observes **Saint‑Jean‑Baptiste Day** (June 24) instead of Family Day.
• Other provinces have their own holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, Heritage Days, etc.) that sometimes generate long weekends depending on how they’re scheduled. | | **Other Holidays** | • **Easter Monday** (April 10) is a public holiday in some provinces (Quebec, Ontario, etc.). When it landed on a Monday, it added another long weekend for residents of those provinces.
• **St. Patricks’ Day** (March 16) became a statutory holiday in Newfoundland & Labrador, producing a short long weekend (Fri Mar 10–Mon Mar 13). | | **Christmas / Boxing Day** | These holidays did NOT automatically create long weekends in 2023—Christmas fell on Monday and Boxing Day on Tuesday. Employees who took Fridays off around the holidays turned the period into a five‑day break, but it wasn’t mandated by law. | | **Holiday Observances** | Whenever a holiday falls on a weekend, the government usually designates the nearest weekday as the observance day (as seen with New Year’s Day and Canada Day above). Those observation days count toward the long‑weekend tally. | --- #### Quick Takeaway for Your App If your goal is to flag all potential long‑holiday periods for users across Canada, you’ll want to: 1. Include the **national holidays listed above**, noting where they apply provincially. 2. Add **province‑specific holidays** (like St. Patrick’s Day, Heritage Days, etc.), especially if your target audience lives in those regions. 3. Highlight that **removing a single workday** (often a Friday) can extend a holiday into a full week‑off, even though the legal holiday isn’t on a weekend. Feel free to let me know if you’d like a more granular breakdown per province or integration tips!
